name: crowdbricks (batched NVIDIA MotionBricks)
summary: Apache-2.0 add-on by Patch that runs NVIDIA MotionBricks with a batch dimension (TensorRT plan + batched SOMA kernels) plus a light crowd runtime (drivers, gaits, obstacles, recorder, web viewer). README benchmark on an RTX 4090 FP16: 389 generations/s one at a time vs 10,307/s at batch 48 (~26x); 192-character horde steps in 2.4 ms. Tests check it matches upstream. Leaves out upstream's hand/foot IK, idle/sit clips and input springs.

access.notes: Code Apache-2.0, but ships no models: needs a MotionBricks checkout and NVIDIA GPU. Weights under NVIDIA Open Model Agreement; gaits/obstacle targets come from sample clips under NVIDIA Sample Data Evaluation License (eval-only), so check before shipping. No hand/foot IK.

procedure: Set up NVlabs/motionbricks first: git clone https://github.com/NVlabs/motionbricks, git lfs pull, uv sync (NVIDIA GPU, Git LFS, uv).
git clone https://github.com/patch-gg/crowdbricks next to it.
export PYTHONPATH=$PWD/../motionbricks and run ../motionbricks/.venv/bin/python examples/futures.py --record futures.take (first run builds a TensorRT plan, a few minutes).
View takes: run viewer/export_character.py once, serve the folder with python3 -m http.server 8000, open /viewer/?take=../futures.take.

stats.count: 1 repo, single initial commit (Oct 27 2026), no tagged release

verdict.why: Clear README, reproducible benchmarks and an upstream-match test; real speedup for crowds. Brand new (one commit), needs an NVIDIA GPU and the MotionBricks checkout, no IK, and its out-of-box gaits rely on eval-only sample data, so commercial use is restricted.
